result:
Compiled successfully.

I inspected the javadoc spec for `NumberUtils` and wrote `tests/org/apache/commons/lang3/math/NumberUtilsAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 4 test class covering:

- Reusable wrapper constants (BYTE/SHORT/INTEGER/LONG/FLOAT/DOUBLE ZERO/ONE/MINUS_ONE)
- `toByte/toShort/toInt/toLong/toFloat/toDouble` (1-arg and default-value overloads), including null, empty, invalid, and out-of-range boundary cases
- `createNumber` (null, plain/negative ints, type qualifiers L/F/D, hex, non-octal leading zero, invalid/empty/untrimmed strings throwing `NumberFormatException`)
- `createFloat/createDouble/createInteger/createLong/createBigInteger/createBigDecimal` (null handling, valid conversion, hex/octal distinction for `createInteger`, invalid-input exceptions)
- array `min`/`max` for all 6 primitive types, including null/empty `IllegalArgumentException` cases
- 3-argument `min`/`max` overloads for all 6 primitive types, plus documented NaN and Infinity handling for `double`/`float`
- `isDigits` and `isNumber` boundary/error cases
- the public no-arg constructor

One note: I could not inspect `lib/` per the task restrictions, and the sandbox blocks running `java` (only `javac` is permitted), so I relied solely on `api/org/apache/commons/lang3/math/NumberUtils.html` as the contract source, as required. `./compile.sh` reports `compiled OK`.
